source.version: Working paper dated August 2026 (OpenAI-hosted report PDF, 49 pages). The retrieval record says it matches CEPR Discussion Paper 21882 (title, authors, abstract); the CEPR PDF was not compared. The main text anonymizes the university (footnote 2, p. 2), but the appendix and the case text name Bocconi.
source.title_on_document: Training novices to think, or giving them LLMs? Evidence from an RCT

supplement.where: No external supplement or online appendix is referenced. The Appendix (Sections 1 to 6, Tables A.1 to A.14) is part of this PDF, printed pp. 16-48 (PDF pp. 17-49). The pre-analysis plan is registered with the AEA RCT Registry, but the link and number are withheld for anonymity (footnote 2, p. 2; Appendix p. 16).
supplement.holds: Nothing outside this PDF. All coefficient tables with clustered standard errors (Tables A.9-A.14), descriptive statistics (Table A.7) and balance checks (Table A.8) are in the appendix of this PDF. Arm-level means and SDs of the outcomes are not reported anywhere.

paper_design_summary: A 2x2 factorial trial at a European university (Bocconi) randomized 13 intact first-year management classes (1,053 undergraduates) to causal-reasoning training or a placebo game, crossed with ChatGPT Edu (GPT-4o) access or none, during regular class time. All students then wrote a recommendation of about 180 words on how to raise alumni awareness and usage of the university's merchandise. Trained master's-student raters scored the recommendations on a 1-5 awareness-and-usage rubric, and LLM pipelines measured similarity to three expert texts, the number of distinct core ideas, and the embedding diversity of ideas within and between participants.

studies.label: 2x2 classroom RCT: causal-reasoning training x ChatGPT Edu access, merchandising business case

assignment.what_was_assigned: Each intact class section to one of four conditions: placebo game without ChatGPT (Control), causal-reasoning training game without ChatGPT (Causal), placebo game with ChatGPT Edu access (GPT), training game with ChatGPT Edu access (Causal&GPT). One class per program per arm; in the Management program (5 classes) two classes went to the Causal&GPT arm.
assignment.quote: We randomized at the classroom level within program to one of four conditions: causal reasoning training versus a placebo game, and ChatGPT Edu access versus none: Control, Causal, GPT, and Causal&GPT
assignment.locator: p. 1 (PDF p. 2), Section 1; Appendix Section 1, p. 16 (PDF p. 17)
assignment.prereg_locator: Appendix Section 1, p. 16 (PDF p. 17): 'The study was pre-registered with the AEA RCT Registry [link currently not available to preserve anonymity] prior to data collection'; footnote 2, p. 2

arms.name: Control
arms.description: Placebo game (same 12 questions, no scaffolding or feedback), no ChatGPT during the case

arms.name: Causal
arms.description: Causal-reasoning training game (12 binary-choice questions with worked examples and feedback), reminder prompt before the case, no ChatGPT

arms.name: GPT
arms.description: Placebo game, then ChatGPT Edu (GPT-4o) available in a separate browser tab during the case

arms.name: Causal&GPT
arms.description: Causal-reasoning training game plus reminder prompt, then ChatGPT Edu (GPT-4o) available during the case

participants.exclusions: No exclusions are described. Assignment was by class; the 1,053 are the students who attended the unannounced class sessions ('participation in the experiment reflected regular class attendance', p. 2), and the paper does not report enrolment or absences in the 13 classes. The abstract states 'we assign 1,053 first-year undergraduates'. Arm sizes 249/256/197/351 are given in the text (p. 1) and Table A.8. All outcome regressions use 1,053 observations except within-solution idea diversity (1,051: two responses had only one core idea and were set to missing, p. 41). Footnote 1 (p. 1): 90.5% of participants with GPT access declared compliance (88% GPT only, 92% Causal&GPT); non-compliers are kept in the analysis as far as the paper shows.
participants.who: First-year undergraduates in 13 class sections of the same introductory Management course across three bachelor programs (economics & management, economics & finance, management)
participants.country: Italy (Bocconi University, Milan, is named in the appendix and the case text; the main text says 'a leading European university')
participants.quote: In a 2×2 randomized control trial, we assign 1,053 first-year undergraduates in economics, management and finance to one of four conditions
participants.locator: Abstract (PDF p. 1); p. 1 (PDF p. 2) for arm sizes; Table A.8, p. 42 (PDF p. 43)

ai_tool.how_used: Participants in the AI arms could use ChatGPT Edu in a separate browser tab while writing the case recommendation in Qualtrics; non-AI arms were not allowed to use it (p. 6; Appendix p. 17). AI-arm participants were invited to share their conversation logs afterwards.

task.description: Consultant-style business recommendation of about 180 words on how to increase alumni awareness and usage of the university's branded merchandise, given operational data on sales channels, pricing and the 144,000+ alumni base
task.duration: About 45 minutes (main text: 'spent 45 minutes on a real-world business case', p. 2; Appendix p. 16: each session, including surveys and the game, lasted approximately 45 minutes)

outcomes.name: Awareness and usage evaluation score
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Twenty trained master's students (mostly management programs; the paper calls them 'human experts') blind to condition; each response scored by three raters on two 1-5 rubric attributes (awareness, usage); score = mean over three raters of each rater's (awareness+usage)/2. ICC overall 0.544 (Table A.3). Robustness: OLS with and without balance controls (Table A.10) and PDS Lasso variants that add mediating controls (Table A.13).

contrasts.reported: OLS, SEs clustered by mother tongue x high-school type x degree class. No controls: GPT 0.834*** (0.100), Causal -0.101 (0.068), Causal x GPT 0.072 (0.125), constant 2.236 (0.040). With balance controls: GPT 0.862*** (0.079), Causal -0.111*** (0.040), Causal x GPT 0.082 (0.084), constant 2.089 (0.230); N = 1053. Full-sample DV mean 2.635, SD 0.843 (Table A.7). Causal&GPT vs Causal equals GPT + interaction; no single coefficient is printed.
contrasts.locator: Table A.10, p. 44 (PDF p. 45); Figure 3, p. 8; text p. 7; Table A.7, p. 41

outcomes.name: Number of ideas in the solution (core ideas)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Count of distinct core ideas from an LLM extraction pipeline (GPT-5.2, three prompt variants x five runs plus one pass; ideas confirmed in at least 2 of 16 runs; uncertain matches judged by GPT-5.2 and Claude Opus 4.6). Full-sample mean 6.756, SD 3.170. Figure 5 shows the coefficient in SD units.

contrasts.reported: OLS with balance controls, SEs clustered (50 clusters): GPT 2.251*** (0.290), Causal 0.348* (0.194), Causal x GPT 0.690* (0.357), constant 4.118 (1.031); N = 1053. Text: GPT raises the number of core ideas 'by more than one-half of a standard deviation'.
contrasts.locator: Table A.12 col. 1, p. 45 (PDF p. 46); Figure 5 and text, p. 10; Table A.7, p. 41

outcomes.name: Within-solution diversity of ideas
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Mean pairwise cosine distance (text-embedding-3-large) among the core ideas within one participant's response; missing for 2 responses with a single core idea (N = 1,051). Full-sample mean 0.596, SD 0.078.

contrasts.reported: OLS with balance controls, SEs clustered (50 clusters): GPT 0.009** (0.005), Causal 0.043*** (0.006), Causal x GPT -0.001 (0.008), constant 0.541 (0.025); N = 1051. Text: GPT 'also has a positive but much smaller effect' than Causal (about one-half SD).
contrasts.locator: Table A.12 col. 2, p. 45 (PDF p. 46); Figure 5 and text, p. 10; Section 4 of Appendix, p. 41

outcomes.name: Between-solution diversity of ideas
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Mean cosine distance (text-embedding-3-large) of a participant's core ideas from all other participants' ideas in the full pooled sample (1,052 other responses). Higher = more distinct from others; no sign reversal needed. Full-sample mean 0.624, SD 0.038.

contrasts.reported: OLS with balance controls, SEs clustered (50 clusters): GPT -0.002 (0.002), Causal 0.018*** (0.003), Causal x GPT 0.002 (0.004), constant 0.597 (0.010); N = 1053. Text: 'GPT alone and the interaction between Causal and GPT are not distinguishable from zero.'
contrasts.locator: Table A.12 col. 3, p. 45 (PDF p. 46); Figure 5 and text, p. 10

contrasts.reported: No single coefficient printed; the contrast equals GPT (-0.002, SE 0.002) plus Causal x GPT (0.002, SE 0.004). Text: 'relative to Causal alone, adding the availability of LLMs does not increase diversity, but it does not kill it either.'
contrasts.locator: Table A.12 col. 3, p. 45 (PDF p. 46); Conclusions, p. 13 (PDF p. 14)

diversity_detail.metric: Mean cosine distance between each participant's core-idea embeddings and the ideas of all other participants
diversity_detail.embedding_model: OpenAI text-embedding-3-large (Italian responses translated to English during extraction)
diversity_detail.computed_over: Each participant's ideas against all other participants' ideas in the whole sample, pooled across all four arms (not within arm); one score per participant
diversity_detail.uncertainty: OLS of participant-level scores on treatment dummies with balance controls; SEs clustered by mother tongue x high-school type x degree class (50 clusters), not by the 13 randomized classes
diversity_detail.notes: Because the reference pool is the whole sample, this measures distance from the overall solution space, not within-arm homogeneity. The paper reports no within-arm pairwise similarity.

outcomes.name: Similarity of participant solution with expert solutions (Marketing professor, Merchandising expert, Expert alumnus)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: 1 minus cosine distance (text-embedding-3-large) between each response and each of three expert-written solutions, in the participant's survey language; three separate dependent variables. Full-sample means 0.794 / 0.753 / 0.806, SDs 0.041 / 0.045 / 0.050. Robustness: with and without balance controls (Table A.11), PDS Lasso (Table A.14). Measures closeness to expert answers, not novelty.

contrasts.reported: GPT coefficient, no controls / with balance controls: Mkt Professor 0.028*** (0.007) / 0.026*** (0.004); Merchandising expert 0.030*** (0.007) / 0.028*** (0.005); Expert Alumnus 0.044*** (0.006) / 0.044*** (0.005). Causal and Causal x GPT not significant in any column. N = 1053.
contrasts.locator: Table A.11, p. 44 (PDF p. 45); Figure 4, p. 9

company_involvement.description: Two authors are affiliated with OpenAI (Asirvatham; Chatterji, OpenAI & Duke); Rachel Brown contributed during her employment at OpenAI; Steve Ramos contributed as a paid contractor for OpenAI. The AI tool is OpenAI's ChatGPT Edu, and the outcome pipelines use OpenAI models (GPT-5, GPT-5.2, text-embedding-3-large). The PDF on file is hosted on cdn.openai.com (retrieval record).
company_involvement.locator: Title page (PDF p. 1), author affiliations and footnotes

eligibility.reason: ChatGPT Edu access was randomly assigned at the class level (13 classes, one per program per arm, two for Causal&GPT in Management) with no-AI comparison arms; 1,053 students analyzed (197 GPT vs 249 Control for the main contrast). Outcomes are scored on the written recommendations: a rater-scored usefulness rubric, idea counts, and embedding diversity of ideas across participants. Caveats: randomization of only 13 clusters with several balance failures, SEs clustered on 50 cells rather than the 13 randomized classes, and the task is a business recommendation judged on a codified marketing rubric rather than on originality.

one_line_finding: ChatGPT access raised the rater-scored awareness-and-usage score by 0.862 points on a 1-5 scale (SE 0.079; control constant 2.089) and the number of core ideas by 2.251 (SE 0.290), but left between-participant idea diversity unchanged (-0.002, SE 0.002) (Tables A.10 and A.12, pp. 44-45).
open_questions: Design class: the experiment ran in regular class sessions of a required course under proctor supervision, unannounced and ungraded as far as the paper says. I coded field_rct (inside coursework); lab_rct (supervised session) is also defensible.

Randomization is of 13 intact classes, but SEs are clustered by mother tongue x high-school type x degree class (50 clusters). A pooled SE that reflects the randomization unit would need class-level clustering, which the paper does not report.

The paper does not say how many enrolled students were absent from the unannounced sessions, so n_randomized at the class level is not known; 1,053 is the number in the analysis and the number the abstract says was assigned.
Arm-level means and SDs of outcomes are not reported; only full-sample SDs (Table A.7) and regression coefficients. Figure 5 and Figure 2 show coefficients in SD units graphically.
The between-solution diversity measure is computed against the whole pooled sample, not within arm, so it is not a within-condition homogenization measure.
Rater type: the 20 raters are trained master's students in management whom the paper calls 'human experts'; I coded human_raters.
notes: Outcomes omitted from the outcome list because they are not creativity or diversity: LLM-scored causal-reasoning attributes of the text (coherent logic, falsifiability, mechanisms; Table A.9, GPT coefficients -0.008, 0.029, 0.214***), game time and score (pre-AI), text-complexity measures used as controls, and self-reported post-treatment attitudes. Within-arm inter-rater ICC is higher in the GPT arm (0.534) than in Control (0.275) (Table A.3, p. 22). Table A.7 lists CRT mean 0.490 while Table A.8 lists 0.769 for the total sample, an internal inconsistency not affecting outcomes. ai_available_when_produced is 'yes' for all outcomes: the treatment arms wrote the scored text with ChatGPT open in a separate tab.
